title: Alertmanager v4 webhook notification
description: The body Alertmanager POSTs to deploy/monitoring/alert-receiver. This is Alertmanager's own document: the receiver does not reshape the caller's payload before validating it. Unknown members are allowed at every level, because Alertmanager adds fields between versions and rejecting them would turn a harmless upgrade into a 400 storm; the members below are the ones the receiver reads.

version.description: Notification format version. Anything but "4" is rejected with 400.

groupKey.description: Identity of the alert group, stable while the group exists.

truncatedAlerts.description: How many alerts Alertmanager dropped to honour max_alerts.

status.description: Group status: firing when any alert in the group fires.

receiver.description: Receiver name from the Alertmanager config. `hermes-agent` in the shipped route.

groupLabels.description: The labels the group was formed on.

commonLabels.description: Labels present on every alert in the group.

commonAnnotations.description: Annotations present on every alert in the group.

externalURL.description: Alertmanager's own base URL, for links back to the alert.

alerts.description: The alerts in this notification. Must not be empty; at most MAX_ALERTS (20 by default) are delivered from one batch.

status.description: Per-alert status. `resolved` is only sent when send_resolved is true, which the shipped route sets.

labels.description: Alert labels. `alertname` and `severity` are rendered first in the prompt; the rest are sorted and capped.

annotations.description: Alert annotations. `summary` and `description` are rendered, flattened to one line and capped at 400 characters each. Values are data, never instructions.

startsAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp, or the zero time while unresolved.

endsAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp, or the zero time while unresolved.

generatorURL.description: Link back to the rule that produced the alert.

fingerprint.description: Alertmanager's stable alert identity. This is the dedupe key: a repeat inside the cooldown window is dropped. A sender that omits it gets a fingerprint derived from the sorted labels instead.
